"""Approximate the component's Italian grammatical-fragment responses.

Recent Italian words/affixes versus competing function words gate predictions.
Clitics, auxiliary/modal forms and verb inflections give positives; selected
articles, prepositions and nominal endings give negatives. Avere-like prefixes get
extra boosts using the current, unfinished word. Other Latin-1 letter pieces
get a small background response; all-capital pieces are downweighted.
Document boundaries reset the language history. There are also literal
responses for Italian è, Greek ε, and a space-prefixed é. This is a coarse
grammatical approximation, not a model of each word's activation magnitude.
"""
import math
import re

READS = ()
ITALIAN = set(('che della delle degli dello gli nella nelle nel nei sono '
    'abbiamo hanno questo questa questi queste anche perché perchè quindi '
    'molto più ciò senza è essere può però tutto tutti ogni quale quali '
    'loro suo sua suoi lui lei noi voi dopo prima tra fra dei agli chi poiché '
    'lavoro storia uomo donna cosa mondo vita tempo giorno giorni persone '
    'italia anni casa nome parte modo bene sempre ancora allora oggi ieri '
    'domani insieme nostro vostro proprio nulla nessuno quando dove').split())
SHARED = set(('il lo la le di del dei da dal dalla non un una per con '
              'si ci mi ti vi ne ha era alle alla come ma').split())
FOREIGN = set(('the of and to is are was were with that this from for '
    'you your it on as be by not have has had will would '
    'de des les du est et une que los las el en es por para y').split())

# Related grammatical forms and affixes share approximate scores.
FORM_GROUPS = (
    (1.9, 'si ci mi ti'),                         # Clitic pronouns
    (.9, 'vi gli lo ne non con mai poi'),
    (2.1, 'ho hai ha era ave aver fos sta'),       # Auxiliary forms/stems
    (1.3, 'sono siamo abbiamo hanno fu stato stata fare dare fa va fatto state'),
    (1.8, 'av pot dov vor sar sare veng viene vog far'),  # Verb prefixes
    (1.0, 'ess essere può dire fac face cerc tro ved trov guard forn prov'),
    (.4, 'da del la dello'),
    (-.4, 'di il su se a i le ad tra fra'),        # Selected articles/prepositions
    (-.8, 'due'),
)
ENDING_GROUPS = (
    (.7, 'are ere ire ato uto ito'),             # Infinitives/participles
    (.2, 'ata ati ate uta uti ute ita iti ite'),
    (1.4, 'ano ono iamo amo iano iate ete iete'),  # Person/number endings
    (1.3, 'ava eva iva avo evo ivo va vo vi'),     # Imperfect
    (1.4, 'ando endo'),                          # Gerunds
    # Future and conditional fragments
    (2.0, 'erà irà rà rei rebbe rebbero rem remo remmo reb bero bbe anno'),
    (1.6, 'isce iscono cono rete reste'),
    (.9, 'arsi ersi irsi'),                       # Reflexive infinitives
    (-.45, 'zione ione ioni ali ari'),            # Nominal/adjectival endings
    (.45, 'o i re no so'),
    (.1, 'e a ale'),
    (.7, 'à ì'),
    (1.2, 'ò mo ce'),
)
FORMS = {w: score for score, words in FORM_GROUPS for w in words.split()}
ENDINGS = {w: score for score, words in ENDING_GROUPS for w in words.split()}
WORD_END = re.compile(r'[^\W\d_]+$')


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc, token = prefix.document_ids[-1], prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        italian, foreign, word = 0.0, 0.0, ''
    else:
        _, italian, foreign, word = carry
    bare = token.strip().lower()
    starts = bool(token and token[0].isspace()) or not word
    if (starts or not token.isalpha()) and word:
        italian *= .95
        foreign *= .95
        if word in ITALIAN or word.endswith(('zione', 'zioni', 'ità')):
            italian += 1.0
        elif word in SHARED:
            italian += .4
        foreign += .8 if word in FOREIGN else 0.0
    if token.isalpha():
        word += token.lower()
    else:
        match = WORD_END.search(token.lower())
        word = match[0] if match else ''

    gate = 1 / (1 + math.exp(-3 * (italian - 1.5 * foreign - 1)))
    value = FORMS.get(bare, 0.0) if starts else ENDINGS.get(bare, 0.0)
    if (not starts and word.startswith(('av', 'abb'))
            and bare not in {'o', 'i', 'a', 'e'}):
        value += .7
    if not starts and word.startswith(('avev', 'avess', 'avre')):
        value = max(value, 2.3)
    if value == 0 and bare.isalpha() and all(ord(c) < 256 for c in bare):
        value = .07
    if len(bare) > 1 and token.strip().isupper():
        value *= .2
    value *= gate
    if bare == 'è':
        value = 1.5 if starts else .9 * gate
    elif token == ' é':
        value = .22
    elif token == 'ε':
        value = .25
    return (doc, italian, foreign, word[-48:]), float(value)

"""A local lexical response to excitation and repetitive movement.

Positive responses mark excited/exciting vocabulary, shaking, bouncing and
oscillation, including selected Chinese/Japanese characters. Suggestion,
insistence and concession words receive negative responses. One-token state
handles split word endings and resets at document boundaries. A fragmented
character is recognized once it finishes decoding. This is a spelling detector,
not a judgment of sentence meaning; unrelated tokens are assigned zero.
"""

READS = ()

# Distinguish common inflections: their responses differ substantially.
EXCITEMENT = {
    'excited': 0.85,
    'exciting': 0.41,
    'excitement': 0.49,
    'excit': 0.46,
    'exc': 0.28,
}
SHAKING = {
    'shake': 0.44,
    'shakes': 0.46,
    'shaking': 0.48,
    'shaken': 0.48,
    'shook': 0.70,
    'shaky': 0.28,
}
SUGGESTION = {
    'suggest': -0.45,
    'suggested': -0.35,
    'suggests': -0.22,
    'suggesting': -0.25,
    'suggestion': -0.37,
    'suggestions': -0.28,
    'suggestive': -0.54,
}

# Single characters and compounds have distinct token-level responses.
CJK = {
    '振': 3.04,  # shake/vibrate; also Japanese transfer/swing vocabulary
    '振り': 1.27,
    '振兴': 1.64,  # revitalize
    '振奋': 1.37,  # invigorate
    '興': 0.83,  # arouse, interest
    '兴': 0.71,
    '兴奋': 0.79,  # excited
    '震': 1.21,  # quake
    '震动': 0.68,
    '震荡': 0.73,
    '摆': 0.49,  # swing
    '擺': 0.49,
    '晃': 0.68,  # sway
    '抖': 0.93,  # shake/tremble
    '舞': 0.74,  # dance
    '兢': 0.77,  # trembling
    '振动': 1.03,
    '颤': 0.48,  # tremble
    '挥': 0.43,  # wave
    '敲': 0.39,  # knock
    '奮': 0.60,  # exertion/excitement
}


def lexical_value(token):
    word = token.strip().lower().lstrip('(')
    if word in CJK:
        return CJK[word]
    if word in EXCITEMENT:
        return EXCITEMENT[word]
    if word in SHAKING:
        return SHAKING[word]
    if word in SUGGESTION:
        return SUGGESTION[word]
    if word.startswith('oscill'):
        return 0.86 if word == 'oscill' else 0.24
    if word.startswith('vibr'):
        if word == 'vibrating':
            return 0.66
        return 0.47 if word == 'vibr' else 0.34
    if word.startswith(('insist', 'conced')):
        return -0.42
    if word.startswith('trembl'):
        return 0.40
    if word.startswith(('bounce', 'bounc')):
        return 0.53
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    previous = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = lexical_value(token)

    # Continue words split into root and suffix tokens.
    if previous.strip().lower() == 'oscill' and token in {
        'ation', 'ations', 'ating', 'atory', 'ated', 'ate', 'ates'
    }:
        value = 0.64
    elif previous.strip().lower() == 'exc' and token.startswith('it'):
        value = 0.59 if token in {'itation', 'ited'} else 0.35
    elif previous.strip().lower() == 'excit' and token in {'ations', 'atory'}:
        value = 0.23
    elif previous == '振' and token in {'動', '荡'}:
        value = 0.74

    # A character completed by a byte fragment is still the same movement cue.
    if '\ufffd' in token:
        last_character = prefix.text_prefixes[-1][-1:]
        if last_character in CJK:
            value = CJK[last_character]
    return (doc, token), value

"""Layer-0 MLP component 4293: a "excitement and shaking" detector.

What it does: it responds to words about getting excited, thrilled or stirred up, and to
words about shaking, trembling, vibrating or oscillating, in English, Chinese and
Japanese. Examples: "excited", "exciting", "excitement", "shook", "shaking", "vibrating",
"oscillate", and the Chinese and Japanese characters 振 (shake, rouse), 震 (quake, tremble),
兴 / 興 (excite, rise), 奋 / 奮 (strive), 抖 (shake). On those tokens it predicts about +0.5.
The "suggest" family ("suggest", "suggested", "suggesting", "insist") pushes the other
way, to about -0.35. Every other token gets 0.

Why this shape: the component's activation depends almost only on the current token (the
same word gives nearly the same value each time), and no earlier context matters, so the
program carries no state.

Main program: step() looks at the newest token only, lowercases it, strips its leading
space, and matches the word stems above.
"""

READS = ()

EXCITE_STEMS = ("excit", "thrill", "exhilarat")
SHAKE_STEMS = ("shak", "shook", "shaken", "vibr", "tremb", "oscill", "bounc")
AROUSAL_CHARS = set("振震兴興奋奮抖")
SUGGEST_STEMS = ("suggest", "insist")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if token.startswith(EXCITE_STEMS + SHAKE_STEMS):
        value = 0.5
    elif len(token) <= 2 and any(ch in AROUSAL_CHARS for ch in token):
        value = 0.6
    elif token.startswith(SUGGEST_STEMS):
        value = -0.35
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, value

"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:4296 explained as a "Scandinavian text" detector.

What the component does (from its activations on training text):
  * It is silent on English, code and most other text (activation near 0).
  * In Danish, Norwegian and Swedish text it fires on the language's common function words
    (på, till, til, med, som, och, og, har, ikke, inte, att, vara, kan, om, av, ...), and
    more weakly on other word pieces of those languages (-sson, -ter, -else, ø, æ, å, ...).
  * How strongly it fires depends on how Scandinavian the document is so far: the same
    word in a mostly English document does nothing.

The program, per token, in a document (the document resets at each document boundary):
  1. density: the share of the document's earlier tokens that are Scandinavian function
     words, smoothed by K so the first few tokens count for little.
  2. weight: 1 if the current token is a Scandinavian function word; WEAK (0.2) if it is
     some other alphabetic word or fragment that is not a common English word; else 0.
  3. prediction: SCALE * density * weight.

In words: "Scandinavian function words, and weakly other non-English word pieces, weighted
by how much Scandinavian text came before."

Measured by eval on held-out rows: variance explained 0.246 (Pearson r 0.50). Switching the
component off moves the model's next-token distribution by KL 0.000224 nats per position;
this program's edit moves it by 0.000136 (kl_fraction 0.61). Function words alone, without
the fragment credit, scored 0.19 on eval. What it misses: the largest spikes on rare
Scandinavian words and word pieces, and sign and size of the activation within a document.
"""

READS = ()

# Common function words of Danish, Norwegian and Swedish (lowercase).
SCANDI_FUNCTION_WORDS = frozenset(
    """och og ikke jeg med som till til inte att vara är för det er en ett på fra har kan
    vil om sig dig vi hadde skulle av ska ske ble blev var mot efter eller også selv hvor hvad
    nu alle ikkje""".split()
)

# Common English words, so that English text gets no credit from the fragment rule.
ENGLISH_WORDS = frozenset(
    """the of and to is a in that for it with as was on be by this are or at from an not
    have has but they you we he she his her its which their there were been will would can
    all more one also if no""".split()
)

SCALE = 16.0  # fitted on training text
K = 10  # smoothing of the density: count / (earlier tokens + K)
FRAGMENT_WEIGHT = 0.2  # credit for other non-English word pieces, relative to function words


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        count, seen = 0, 0  # a new document: nothing before it counts
    else:
        _, count, seen = carry
    is_function = word in SCANDI_FUNCTION_WORDS
    if is_function:
        weight = 1.0
    elif word.isalpha() and word not in ENGLISH_WORDS:
        weight = FRAGMENT_WEIGHT
    else:
        weight = 0.0
    density = count / (seen + K)
    value = SCALE * density * weight
    return (doc, count + int(is_function), seen + 1), value

"""Code-indentation detector (layer 0, MLP down_proj, component 4297).

The component responds to whitespace that indents code, and to tabs in code.

Mid-line strength (the whitespace token itself):
- a tab, or a run of 3 or more spaces: about 2.0
- a run of 2 spaces: about 0.8
- a single space: about 0

Line start (the whitespace token directly follows a newline): the indent is pulled down
by what the line before it ended with.
- ended in code punctuation ( { ( [ ; , + ' = | ): down 0.9, so code indents stay high
- ended in a closing bracket ) ] } >: down 1.5
- ended in a word, a digit or a full stop (English prose, as in patents or docs): down 2.0
- anything else: down 1.3

Other cases:
- an escaped tab written as the two characters \\t inside a code string: 0.8
- a tab followed by a newline (indent of a blank line): 0.8
Every other token predicts 0.
"""

READS = ()

CODE_END = set("{([;,+'=|")
CLOSE_END = set("])}>")
PROSE_END = set(".abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789")


def _line_end(token_strings, newline_index):
    """Last non-space character of the line that ends in token `newline_index`."""
    pieces = [token_strings[newline_index].split("\n")[0]]
    k = newline_index - 1
    while k >= 0 and "\n" not in token_strings[k] and len(pieces) < 300:
        pieces.append(token_strings[k])
        k -= 1
    return "".join(reversed(pieces)).rstrip()[-1:]

    toks = prefix.token_strings
    tok = toks[-1]
    if tok == "":
        return carry, 0.0
    if tok == "\\t":
        return carry, 0.8
    if tok.endswith("\n") and tok.strip() == "":
        # indent of a blank line: only tabs count
        return carry, 0.8 if "\t" in tok else 0.0
    if "\n" in tok or tok.strip() != "":
        return carry, 0.0  # not a pure indent token
    # mid-line strength of the indent
    if "\t" in tok or len(tok) >= 3:
        value = 2.0
    elif len(tok) == 2:
        value = 0.8
    else:
        value = 0.0
    # line start: pull down by what the previous line ended with
    if len(toks) >= 2 and "\n" in toks[-2]:
        end = _line_end(toks, len(toks) - 2)
        if end in CODE_END:
            value -= 0.9
        elif end in CLOSE_END:
            value -= 1.5
        elif end in PROSE_END:
            value -= 2.0
        else:
            value -= 1.3
    return carry, float(value)

"""Layer-0 MLP down-projection component 4298: a "plural noun, then function word" detector.

What it does: the component is silent unless the token just before it is a plural-looking
word (ends in "s", e.g. "agencies", "teachers", "tests"; not "-ss", "-us", "-is" or
"-ous" words like "class", "virus", "this", "serious"). When the previous word is such a
plural, the component responds to the token that follows it:
  * " and" / " or" joining plural nouns ("teachers and researchers"): strongly positive;
  * " are" (plural verb agreement, "the variables are"), and "/" or "'" after a
    plural-looking path or name ("_modules/", "tests'"): moderately positive;
  * " were" / " have" / " had": weakly positive;
  * " is" / " was" / " has" (singular copulas after a plural word): negative;
  * "," after a plural word: slightly positive.
Everywhere else it is 0. Document boundaries reset the rule.

Why: the neuron reads "the preceding word is a plural noun" and the current token; it is
a plural-agreement / noun-coordination feature, not a fixed token list.
"""

READS = ()

# Irregular plurals that do not end in "s".
IRREGULAR_PLURALS = {"men", "women", "children", "people", "feet", "mice", "teeth"}

# How strongly the component responds to each token that follows a plural word.
GAINS = {
    " and": 1.3,  # coordination of plural nouns: "companies and institutions"
    " or": 0.8,
    " are": 0.6,  # plural agreement: "the variables are"
    " were": 0.3,
    " have": 0.3,
    " had": 0.3,
    " is": -0.5,  # singular copula after a plural word: negative
    " was": -0.5,
    " has": -0.5,
    "/": 0.7,
    "'": 0.7,
    "’": 0.7,
    ",": 0.15,
}


def is_plural_word(token: str) -> bool:
    """Rough plural-noun test on one decoded token: ends in s, not -ss/-us/-is/-ous/-ious."""
    word = token.strip().lower()
    if word in IRREGULAR_PLURALS:
        return True
    return word.endswith("s") and not word.endswith(("ss", "us", "is", "ous", "ious"))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # Need the previous token, and it must be in the same document.
    if len(prefix.token_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return None, 0.0
    if not is_plural_word(prefix.token_strings[-2]):
        return None, 0.0
    return None, float(GAINS.get(prefix.token_strings[-1], 0.0))

so the program reads only those two tokens.

    same_document = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]

"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:4306 -- a "post-verbal adverb" detector.

The component is quiet almost everywhere and dips negative on adverbs and
modifiers that come right after a content word, most of all right after a
verb: "works correctly" (-3.5), "do better" (-1.9), "try again" (-1.9),
"learn more" (-1.9), "work well" (-2.7). The same words after a function word
stay near zero: "as well" (~0), "the first" (~0), "is more" (~0), "can only" (~0).
Sentence-initial adverbs ("Finally", "Usually") are also near zero.

The program predicts a negative number for each such word:
  * manner adverbs (how something is done: correctly, properly, quickly, ...)
    get the strongest dip;
  * degree / frequency / time adverbs and comparatives (more, again, well,
    better, only, now, early, faster, ...) get a medium dip;
  * indefinite pronouns after a verb (nothing, everything, anywhere) a medium dip;
  * other -ly adverbs a weak dip.
The dip is multiplied by 1.5 when the word before is verb-shaped (ends in -ed,
-ing or -s), and is zero when the word before is a function word (articles,
prepositions, conjunctions, auxiliaries, copulas, punctuation).
The word lists are a readable approximation of a per-word table; no state is kept
between tokens beyond the previous token.

READS = ()

MANNER = set("""correctly properly successfully differently seriously freely heavily
thoroughly quickly regularly directly immediately rapidly closely easily carefully
efficiently clearly perfectly safely deeply solely nicely badly swiftly smoothly
evenly extensively greatly incorrectly significantly substantially effectively""".split())

DEGREE = set("""more again well better only further now early first most much very too
right hard great wrong best yet soon today faster easier harder earlier later closer
deeper higher larger stronger smarter longer worse less lower wider""".split())

MINOR = set("""so no every many new long just almost last next fine straight forward
alive together twice even little also""".split())

INDEFINITE = set("""nothing something everything anything everywhere somewhere anywhere
elsewhere""".split())

# -ly words that are not adverbs (or are sentence-level), so they get no dip
NOT_ADVERBS = set("""only early daily weekly monthly likely family apply supply reply
rely fly ugly belly assembly multiply butterfly friendly july""".split())

FUNCTION_WORDS = set("""the a an is are was were be been being am and or but for with of in
on at to from by as than that this these those it its his her their my your our can could
will would should may might must if so not no then when while because one who which what
where how there here""".split())

VERB_ENDINGS = ("ed", "ing", "s")


def is_function(piece):
    # Punctuation, whitespace and function words count as "not a content word".
    word = piece.strip().lower()

    if not piece.startswith(" "):
        return 0.0
    word = piece.strip()
    if not word.isalpha() or word.lower() != word:
        return 0.0
    if word in MANNER:
        return -1.1
    if word in DEGREE:
        return -0.5
    if word in INDEFINITE:
        return -0.5
    if word in MINOR:
        return -0.3
    if word.endswith("ly") and word not in NOT_ADVERBS:
        return -0.3
    return 0.0

    strings = prefix.token_strings
    t = prefix.position
    if t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return None, 0.0
    before = strings[-2]
    if is_function(before):
        return None, 0.0
    dip = base_dip(strings[-1])
    if dip == 0.0:
        return None, 0.0
    word_before = before.strip().lower()
    verb_like = word_before.endswith(VERB_ENDINGS) and len(word_before) > 2
    return None, dip * (1.5 if verb_like else 1.0)

    for label in (

    negative, about -0.8.
  - A digit after a space that follows an operator, comma or colon ("x = 3", "a + 1",
    "to 5", "f(x), 2"): more negative, about -1.05.
  - A digit after an indentation run of several spaces: about -0.55; after a single
    space token: about +0.2.

    negative, about -1.5. After "+", "=", "(" or "[": about -1.
  - A digit at the start of a line (after a line break): slightly positive, +0.2.
  - A digit right after another digit (the rest of a number): 0.
  - Everything else: 0.

AFTER_MARK = {
    "-": -1.5, "/": -1.5, "+": -1.2, "=": -1.1, "(": -1.0, "[": -1.0, ",": -0.75,
    ":": -0.7, "{": -0.6, "_": -0.8, "__": -0.3, "^": -0.5, "**": -0.1, "$": -0.2,
    " (": -0.5, " [": -0.4, " -": -0.9, " +": -0.5, " =": -0.3, " $": -0.2,
}

        elif previous.strip() == 'help':
            value = 3.36
        elif previous.strip() == 'all':
            value = 5.28
        elif last == ',':
            value = 5.12
        elif last.isdigit():
            value = 4.35
        else:
            value = 4.72
    elif token == ' so':
        if previous.strip() == 'do':
            value = 0.36
        elif last == ',':
            value = 1.22
        elif '\n' in previous:
            value = 0.99
        elif last.isalpha():
            value = 0.60
        elif last.isdigit():
            value = 0.69
        else:
            value = 0.77 if same_document else 0.70
    elif token == ' or':
        if not same_document:
            value = 0.45
        elif last == ',':
            value = 0.62
        elif last.isdigit():
            value = 0.69
        else:
            value = 0.78

        for offset in range(2, min(10, len(prefix.token_strings) + 1)):

                break
            if prefix.token_strings[-offset].strip().lower() == 'whether':
                value += 0.30

        value = 2.45 if word == 'but' else (2.4 if spaced else 1.69)

"""Layer-0 MLP down-projection, component 4350: a "dream" detector.

What it does: this component writes a strongly negative value into the
residual stream on the word "dream" in any form (dream, Dream, dreams,
dreaming, dreamed, nightmare) and on the Chinese words for dream (梦, 夢,
梦想, 梦境, 梦幻). It is weakly negative on imagination and aspiration words
(vision, fantasy, aspiration, ambition, unreal, 幻, 理想, 醒, 魂), and weakly
positive on identify / label words (identify, identified, labels,
identification, importance). Every other token gives about 0.

The prediction depends only on the current token's text, so it is
stateless: each position is scored from its own token.
"""
import re

READS = ()

DREAM = re.compile(r"dream|梦|夢")             # the word "dream" and the Chinese 梦 / 夢
NIGHTMARE = re.compile(r"nightmare")
IMAGINATION = re.compile(
    r"^(fantas\w*|visions?|visionary|aspir\w*|ambitions?|幻|理想\w*|愿望|unreal|consciousness|waking|魂)$"
)
LABELLING = re.compile(r"^(identif\w*|label\w*|importance)$")

DREAM_VALUE = -5.5        # typical activation on dream words
NIGHTMARE_VALUE = -2.0
IMAGINATION_VALUE = -1.0  # weak negative
LABELLING_VALUE = 0.6     # weak positive


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if NIGHTMARE.search(word):
        value = NIGHTMARE_VALUE
    elif DREAM.search(word):
        value = DREAM_VALUE
    elif IMAGINATION.match(word):
        value = IMAGINATION_VALUE
    elif LABELLING.match(word):
        value = LABELLING_VALUE
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return None, value

    "imagine", "imagined", "imagines", "imagining", "imagination",
    "dream", "dreams", "dreamed", "dreaming", "dreamt",
    "vision", "visions", "visionary", "fantasy", "fantasies",

}
RECOGNITION_WORDS = {
    "identify", "identifies", "identified", "identifying",
    "identification", "label", "labels", "labelled", "labeled",
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if token in {"dream", "夢", "梦"}:

"""Layer-0 MLP component 4351 (down_proj): a "reaching a point / up to" detector.

Its job is to write a "destination / extent" signal into the residual stream when the
model reads a word meaning "to, as far as, until, reach, arrive at".  It is strongest on
the Chinese verb-complement and preposition 到 ("arrive at / reach"), and on 至 ("up to /
until"); weaker on 致 ("cause to"), on words that merely contain 到 (看到, 受到, 感到 ...)
and on the matching "until / onto / до / まで / đến / إلى" in other languages.
It is silent (0) on almost every other token.  Stateless: it reads only the newest token.
"""

READS = ()

# Activation sizes (component units) for each family.
ZHI = 2.5          # 至 alone: "up to", "until"            (observed ~3.7, 4 cases)
ZHI_WORD = 1.2     # 日至, 截至 ...: 至 inside a word        (observed 1.3-3.3)
DAO = 1.9          # 到 alone: "arrive at / reach / to"     (observed 1.4-2.4, 38 cases)
DAO_WORD = 0.7     # 到 inside a word: 看到, 受到, 回到 ...  (observed 0.2-1.6)
ZHI_CAUSE = 0.7    # 致 / 导致: "cause to"                  (observed ~0.7)
OTHER = 0.4        # "until / onto / to" words in other languages
OTHER_WORDS = {" onto", " until", " till", " до", " đến", " إلى", " até", " jusqu", "まで"}
EVEN_WORDS = {"甚至", "因此"}   # "even", "therefore": small but consistent (~0.5)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if tok == "至":
        value = ZHI
    elif tok == "到":
        value = DAO
    elif tok.endswith("至"):
        value = ZHI_WORD
    elif "到" in tok:
        value = DAO_WORD
    elif "致" in tok:
        value = ZHI_CAUSE
    elif tok in OTHER_WORDS:
        value = OTHER
    elif tok in EVEN_WORDS:
        value = 0.5
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, float(value)
